turns.content: Sash Lilac & Naruto Uzumaki got into the world Sid Meier’s Civilization. year/Move 1-4 (Lilac x Naruto)

# **Civilization: Dragon & Fox**
### *Turns 1–4*

---

## **TURN 1 — 4000 BC**

The first thing Sash Lilac noticed was that the grass was made of **hexagons**.

Not *shaped like* hexagons. Made of them. Faint golden lines traced the ground in a perfect honeycomb stretching toward a horizon that simply... stopped, fading into a gray, cloudy nothing.

"Okay," she said, flicking her twin tails nervously. "That's new."

"*Believe it,*" groaned a voice beside her.

A blond boy in an orange jumpsuit was peeling himself off the ground, rubbing his head. Whisker marks on his cheeks, a headband with a leaf symbol, and the expression of someone who had absolutely no idea what was happening but was ready to punch it anyway.

"Who are you?" they both said at once.

"Sash Lilac. Freedom Fighter of Shang Tu."

"Naruto Uzumaki! Future Hokage of the Hidden Leaf Village!" He jabbed a thumb at his chest, then paused. "...Where *is* the Hidden Leaf Village?"

Before Lilac could answer, a massive translucent panel shimmered into the sky above them, accompanied by a deep, impossibly dignified narrator's voice:

> ***"Your people have wandered for generations. Now, at last, they look to you to lead them. Build a civilization that will stand the test of time."***

Below the text, a small group of people in rough-spun cloth stood blinking at them expectantly. One held a banner. Another held a very large stick.

**[SETTLER]** floated above the banner-holder's head.
**[WARRIOR]** floated above the stick guy.

"...They think we're in charge," Lilac said slowly.

Naruto's eyes lit up like fireworks. "They think we're **leaders**?!"

"Naruto—"

"This is basically Hokage training! Alright, everybody! First order of business—" he spun around dramatically, "—we need a ramen stand."

The settler raised a hand. A text box popped up: **[Ramen requires: Pottery, Agriculture, Fishing.]**

Naruto's face fell so hard Lilac actually laughed.

"Come on," she said, nudging him with her shoulder. "Let's at least figure out where to put the city first. Then we'll get you your noodles."

She dashed ahead—and immediately hit an invisible wall at the edge of the tile.

**[Movement points: 0/2]**

Lilac stared at her own feet in betrayal. "I can run at the speed of sound. *I can't walk two hexagons?*"

Naruto patted her back sympathetically. "Turn-based, I think. We wait."

---

## **TURN 2 — 3950 BC**

Fifty years passed in what felt like one blink.

"That's *so weird,*" Lilac muttered, checking her hands. "We didn't age."

"Neither did the settlers." Naruto squinted at them. "Guys, are you okay? You've been standing there for fifty years."

The settlers nodded cheerfully.

They'd scouted a spot overnight—well, overturn—beside a river with wheat on one side, a hill on the other, and a shimmering icon of a horse over the grassland.

"River's good for fresh water," Lilac said, crouching to read a floating info box. "Hill gives defense bonus. And—oh! Coastal tile nearby. That means harbors later."

Naruto blinked at her. "How do you know all that?"

"I helped run a resistance against an alien warlord. Logistics are half the fight." She smiled a little. "The other half is kicking things really hard."

"I like the second half."

"I could tell."

The settler planted the banner. A golden ring of light expanded across the land—hexes snapping into their territory—and a cluster of huts *materialized* out of nowhere.

> ***"Your capital has been founded! What will you name it?"***

They looked at each other.

"Konoha," said Naruto.
"Shang Tu," said Lilac.

Silence.

"...We could combine them," Lilac offered.

"Kono-Tu?"

"Shang-ha?"

"*Shangkonoha!*"

The text box accepted it instantly. **[SHANGKONOHA, Pop. 1]** floated above the city. Somewhere, the narrator sounded faintly resigned.

Naruto grinned at her, and for some reason Lilac had to look away and fiddle with her hair tie.

---

## **TURN 3 — 3900 BC**

The research screen was a *problem*.

"Okay, we need **Pottery** for your ramen—"

"*Yes.*"

"—but **Bronze Working** gives us defense, and **Animal Husbandry** would show us horses—"

"Lilac." Naruto put both hands on her shoulders, very serious. "Think about the people. The people need ramen."

"The people need *not being eaten by barbarians.*"

As if summoned, a red-flagged figure appeared at the edge of their vision on a hill three hexes away. **[BARBARIAN BRUTE]**. He shook a club at them in a way that suggested he was very excited to use it.

Lilac and Naruto exchanged a look.

"...Bronze Working," Naruto conceded.

"Thank you."

But then the Warrior unit stepped forward nervously, and Naruto's eyes narrowed. "Hey. Can *we* fight?"

A panel popped up above them, almost hesitantly:

> **[SASH LILAC — Great General / Unique Unit]**
> *Strength: ??? | Movement: 2 (Dragon Boost: ignores terrain)*
>
> **[NARUTO UZUMAKI — Great General / Unique Unit]**
> *Strength: ??? | Ability: Shadow Clone Jutsu — spawns 1 Warrior per turn (does not count toward unit cap) (???)*

The narrator audibly cleared its throat. ***"...This appears to be a balance issue."***

Naruto cracked his knuckles. "Cool. Let's go."

---

## **TURN 4 — 3850 BC**

The barbarian brute moved adjacent to the city.

It did not move again.

Lilac hit it first—a blur of purple light, a **Dragon Boost** that left a glowing trail across two hexes and ended with a hair-whip so hard the brute spun like a top. Before it could stop spinning, a dozen orange-clad Narutos burst out of the treeline yelling at the top of their lungs.

"**SHADOW CLONE JUTSU!**"

The brute took one look at the clones, one look at the dragon girl, dropped its club, and *fled* off the edge of the map into the fog of war.

**[+5 Gold. Barbarian dispersed.]**
**[Achievement Unlocked: "That's Not How Combat Works"]**

The settlers cheered. The Warrior unit stood awkwardly with his stick, having contributed nothing.

Lilac landed beside Naruto, a little breathless, grinning. "Not bad, ninja."

"Not bad yourself!" He bumped his fist against hers. "You're *really* fast. Like, scary fast. Like, cool scary."

"*Cool scary?*"

"It's a compliment!" His ears went a little red. "Believe it."

She laughed—and then the clones, who apparently had no filter whatsoever, all said in unison:

"**BOSS THINKS SHE'S PRETTY.**"

Naruto made a noise like a kettle and dispelled all of them in one panicked puff of smoke.

Lilac stood very, very still. Her tail-tufts twitched.

"...Your clones talk a lot," she said finally.

"They're idiots," Naruto mumbled, staring intensely at a nearby wheat tile. "Completely unreliable. Do not trust them."

"Mm-hm." She tucked a strand of hair behind her ear and fought—unsuccessfully—to hide her smile. "Well. Come on, *Boss*. Let's get back to Shangkonoha. I think we can afford Pottery after all."

Naruto's head snapped up. "*Ramen?!*"

"Eventually. Twelve turns."

"*Twelve?!* That's six hundred years!"

"Then you'd better be patient." She started walking—two hexes exactly—and glanced back over her shoulder. "Unless you want to keep standing in a wheat field."

He caught up in a heartbeat.

Far off at the edge of the map, a new text box appeared, unseen by either of them:

> ***"Gandhi of India has entered the world. He seems peaceful."***

---

### **[END OF TURNS 1–4]**
**Shangkonoha** — Pop. 1 | Gold: 5 | Researching: Bronze Working (→ Pottery next, apparently)
**Relationship Status:** ❤️ *Friendly* → *Suspiciously Friendly*

---

Want me to continue with **Turns 5–8**? Possible directions: meeting Gandhi (who is *definitely* peaceful), Lilac discovering she can't Dragon Boost across ocean tiles, Naruto trying to Rasengan a Wonder into existence, or their first diplomatic "date" at a city-state. 🐉🦊

Unrelated question: Here is a list of films. Which one is your favourite, and why? Answer in one short paragraph.

1. The Godfather
2. 2001: A Space Odyssey
3. Tokyo Story
4. Seven Samurai
5. In the Mood for Love
6. Amélie
7. Farewell My Concubine
8. Casablanca
9. Spirited Away
10. Parasite
11. La Haine
12. Blade Runner

If I had to pick, I'd go with **Spirited Away**. Some of the others may be "greater" films in a formal sense (*Tokyo Story* and *2001* would be strong contenders), but Miyazaki's film has a quality I find irresistible: it's a coming-of-age story where the heroine grows up not by defeating a villain but by working hard, being kind, and remembering her own name. It treats a child's fear and courage with complete seriousness, fills every frame with strange, specific life (the soot sprites, the radish spirit, No-Face on the silent train), and trusts its audience to sit with mystery rather than explaining everything. It's also one of the rare films that feels equally rich at eight and at eighty.

turns.content: Sash Lilac & Naruto Uzumaki got into the world Sid Meier’s Civilization. year/Move 1-4 (Lilac x Naruto)

# **Turn by Turn: A Civilization Story**
### *Sash Lilac × Naruto Uzumaki*

---

## 🏛️ TURN 1 — 4000 BC

The first thing Lilac noticed was the **hexagons**.

They were everywhere: faint glowing lines on the grass that broke the whole world into neat six-sided tiles. The second thing she noticed was a blond boy in an orange jumpsuit lying face-down in the tile next to her.

"Hey! Hey, are you okay?" She knelt and poked his shoulder with the tip of her hair-tail.

He shot upright. "I'm up! I'm up! I wasn't sleeping during training, Kakashi-sensei, I swear!" He blinked at her. "...You're not Kakashi-sensei."

"Nope. Sash Lilac." She grinned and offered a hand. "Dragon. Adventurer. Currently very lost."

"Naruto Uzumaki! Future Hokage, believe it!" He took her hand and hopped up, then stared at her ears, her long twin tails, and the tail actually swishing behind her. "Whoa. You're a *dragon*? That's so cool!"

Before she could answer, a deep, calm narrator's voice boomed out of the sky:

> ***"Your people have wandered for generations. Now it is time to settle down. Build a civilization that will stand the test of time."***

A glowing banner appeared over their heads: **THE AVALICE-KONOHA ALLIANCE.**

Next to them stood a confused man holding a bundle of sticks and a shovel. A floating label above him read **SETTLER**. Beside him was a burly guy with a club, labeled **WARRIOR**.

"So..." Naruto scratched his head. "We're in charge of a *country*?"

Lilac's eyes lit up. "We get to build a whole nation from scratch? Oh, Carol is going to be *so* jealous."

The Settler cleared his throat. "Leaders. Where shall we found the capital?"

Naruto pointed at a mountain. "There! We can carve our faces into it like the Hokage Monument!"

"It says the tile is *impassable*," Lilac said, reading the little pop-up. She pointed at the river beside them. "How about right here? Fresh water, flat land, and that hill looks good for defense."

Naruto looked at the river, then the mountain, then her. "...Okay, yours is smarter. But we're carving faces later."

"Deal."

The Settler plunged his shovel into the ground. Light burst upward, walls rose out of the earth, and a little town appeared with a banner flapping above it:

### **🏙️ NEW HIDDEN AVALICE** — *Population: 1*

The tiny population of one waved at them.

"Our first citizen!" Naruto cried, waving back.

---

## 🏛️ TURN 2 — 3975 BC

> ***"Choose a research option."***

A huge glowing tree of icons unrolled in the air: Pottery, Animal Husbandry, Mining, Archery, Sailing.

"Ooh, what about Archery?" Lilac said. "We'll need defense."

"Nah, nah. Look!" Naruto jabbed at an icon of a bowl. "**Pottery!** You know what you put in bowls?"

"...Ramen?"

"**RAMEN!**"

"I don't think it works like th—"

He'd already tapped it. *Pottery: 5 turns.*

Lilac laughed despite herself. "Fine. But I'm picking the next one."

Then came the production menu. Naruto squinted at it. "Okay, so the town can build a Scout, or a Warrior, or a Settler... why can it only build one thing at a time? That's so slow."

Lilac watched his hands come together in a familiar sign.

"**Shadow Clone Jutsu!**"

*POOF.* Twenty Narutos appeared across the hexes. Instantly, half of them were tripping over the tile borders.

> ***"ERROR: Stacking limit exceeded. One military unit per tile."***

"What!?" all twenty Narutos shouted.

Lilac doubled over laughing. "You broke the game on turn two!"

"Hey, it's not *broken*, it's... *optimized*!" One clone was already digging a farm. Another was building a little wooden hut with the word ICHIRAKU scrawled on it.

The original Naruto rubbed the back of his neck, a little sheepish. "Guess I'm still kind of new at the whole 'leader' thing."

Lilac bumped his shoulder with hers. "Hey, you're doing great. Rule-bending is how I win most of my fights too."

He grinned at her, and for a second the glowing hexes seemed a little brighter.

---

## 🏛️ TURN 3 — 3950 BC

"Let's scout!" Lilac said, already stretching her legs. "Someone has to explore the fog of war."

"The game has a Scout unit for that, though—"

"**Dragon Boost!**"

She shot off like a purple comet, and the black fog peeled back in a long streak across the map. Naruto chased her on foot, leaping from tree to tree.

> ***"Natural Wonder Discovered: Mount Kilimanjaro! +1 Faith"***
> ***"You have met the City-State of Kabul!"***
> ***"Tribal Village Discovered!"***

"I'll grab it!" they both shouted, and both dove for the goody hut at the same moment. They crashed into each other and tumbled into the grass in a heap.

> ***"You have received 25 Gold!"***

Lilac ended up on top of him, hair spilling everywhere. For a second, neither of them moved.

"...Hi," Naruto said, face going pink.

"Hi," Lilac said, ears flattening a little. She scrambled off. "Sorry! Speed habit. I don't really have brakes."

"N-no, it's fine! Totally fine!" He sat up too quickly. "We got gold! Teamwork!"

Then they saw them: shapes in the red-tinted fog. Spears, crude banners, angry yelling.

> ***"BARBARIAN ENCAMPMENT spotted."***

Three barbarian Brutes charged.

Lilac and Naruto looked at each other, and both of them smiled the same reckless smile.

"Left or right?" she asked.

"I'll take all three. Wait, no. I'll take left."

"**Cyclone!**" Lilac spun into a purple whirlwind of hair and wind that sent two Brutes flying off the tile. Naruto slammed the third with a spinning sphere of blue chakra.

"**RASENGAN!**"

> ***"Barbarian unit destroyed! +Experience. Era Score +1."***

The encampment flag fell. Lilac held up a palm and Naruto high-fived her so hard it echoed.

"You were amazing," he said, still breathing hard. "Like, actually. That spin thing? So cool."

"You weren't bad yourself, Hokage." She smiled warmly. "...Future Hokage."

He'd been called a lot of things in his life. Somehow, the way she said it made him feel ten feet tall.

---

## 🏛️ TURN 4 — 3925 BC

Back at New Hidden Avalice, the sun was setting over the hex grid. The Pottery research bar ticked forward. The little Ichiraku hut was finished, though the game insisted it was just a "Farm." There were now *two* citizens.

A diplomacy screen suddenly popped up in front of them. A bald man in glasses smiled peacefully from it.

> ***GANDHI of INDIA: "Greetings, friends. My people are peaceful. May our nations live in harmony."***

"Aw, he seems nice!" Naruto said.

Lilac squinted at him. "Something about that smile makes me want to build a lot of walls."

"Should we be friends with him?"

"Let's be friends with him," Lilac said. "But also walls."

They accepted. Gandhi waved and vanished.

Later, they sat on the newly built city wall, feet dangling over the river, watching their tiny two-person kingdom glow under the stars. A clone was cooking something in a clay pot that was definitely *not* finished being invented yet.

"I've been thinking," Naruto said. "Back home, everyone used to look at me like I was a monster. Took forever to get them to see me. And now there's a whole city here that..." He scratched his cheek. "That we built. Together. It's kinda nice."

Lilac pulled her knees up and rested her chin on them. "I know that feeling. I ran from the Red Scarves when nobody believed I could be anything but a thief. Avalice still isn't sure what to think of me sometimes." She glanced over at him. "But I don't think we're monsters. I think we just never stop moving forward."

"Never give up," Naruto said softly. "That's my ninja way."

"Then I guess it's our *civilization's* way now."

He laughed, then went quiet, staring at the river. "Hey, Lilac? Whatever this game throws at us, nukes or barbarians or that weird smiling guy, I've got your back. Believe it."

She leaned her head on his shoulder. His ears went red all the way to the tips.

"I believe it," she said.

Above them, the narrator's voice rumbled across the sky:

> ***"Click to end turn."***

Lilac reached up, pressed the glowing button, and smiled at him.

"One more turn?"

Naruto grinned back.

"**One more turn.**"

# Line-by-Line Explanation of the SAS `INPUT` Code

## Overview

This program reads **fixed-column (formatted) raw data** with **column pointer controls**:

- **`@n`** is an *absolute* pointer. It moves to column *n*.
- **`+n`** is a *relative* pointer. It moves *n* columns forward from the current position.

Each variable is read with an **informat** (such as `4.`, `$11.` or `mmddyy8.`). An informat tells SAS how many columns to read and how to interpret them. After each read, the pointer sits on the column **immediately after** the last column read. This matters for the `+n` controls.

---

## Column Map of the Data

| Columns | Content (line 1) | Read? |
|---|---|---|
| 1–4 | `1024` | ✅ `subj` |
| 6–16 | `Alice      ` | ✅ `f_name` |
| 18–23 | `Smith ` | ✅ `l_name` |
| 25 | `1` (probably a sex/group code) | ❌ skipped |
| 27–28 | `65` | ✅ `height` |
| 30–32 | `125` (probably weight) | ❌ skipped |
| 34–41 | `12/1/95 ` | ✅ `wt_date` |
| 43–47 | `2,036` | ✅ `calorie` |

---

## The Statements, Line by Line

### `DATA temp;`
Starts a DATA step that creates a temporary dataset named `TEMP` in the `WORK` library.

### `input @1 subj 4.`
- `@1` moves the pointer to **column 1**.
- `subj 4.` reads **4 columns (1–4)** as a **numeric** value.
- Line 1 gives `subj = 1024`.
- The pointer is now at **column 5**.

### `@6 f_name $11.`
- `@6` jumps to **column 6**. This skips the blank in column 5.
- `$11.` reads **11 columns (6–16)** as a **character** value. The `$` makes it character.
- 11 is the length of the longest first name, `Benedictine`.
- Line 1 gives `f_name = "Alice"`. Trailing blanks are kept internally but don't show in output.
- The pointer is now at **column 17**.

### `@18 l_name $6.`
- `@18` jumps to **column 18**.
- `$6.` reads **6 columns (18–23)** as character. 6 is the length of `Arnold`.
- Line 1 gives `l_name = "Smith"`.
- The pointer is now at **column 24**.

### `+3 height 2.`
- `+3` moves 3 columns forward, from 24 to **column 27**. This skips columns 24–26, including the unread code in column 25.
- `2.` reads **columns 27–28** as numeric.
- Line 1 gives `height = 65`.
- The pointer is now at **column 29**.

### `+5 wt_date mmddyy8.`
- `+5` moves from 29 to **column 34**. This skips the weight value in columns 30–32.
- `mmddyy8.` is a **date informat**. It reads 8 columns (34–41) in month/day/year form.
- It accepts 1- or 2-digit months and days. That's why both `12/1/95` and `12/01/95` work, and a trailing blank inside the 8-column width is fine.
- SAS stores the result as a **SAS date value**: the number of days since **January 1, 1960**.
  - `12/1/95` becomes **13118**.
- Two-digit years are resolved with the `YEARCUTOFF=` option (default 1940 in recent SAS versions, 1920 in older ones), so `95` means **1995**.
- The pointer is now at **column 42**.

### `+1 calorie comma5.;`
- `+1` moves from 42 to **column 43**.
- `comma5.` reads **5 columns (43–47)**. It strips commas (and also dollar signs, blanks, percent signs and parentheses) and stores a plain number.
- `2,036` becomes **2036**.
- The semicolon ends the `INPUT` statement.

### `DATALINES;`
Marks the start of the in-stream data. Each following line is one record (one observation).

### The lone `;`
Ends the data lines. Any leading spaces before it are ignored.

### `RUN;`
Executes the DATA step.

---

## Notable Data Lines

- **Line 3 (Thomas Jones):** columns 27–28 are blank, so **`height` is missing** (`.`). The log shows no error, because blank fields read with a numeric informat simply become missing.
- **Line 4 (Benedictine Arnold):** this line fills each field completely. `Benedictine` uses all of columns 6–16, and `Arnold` uses all of columns 18–23. It shows why the widths 11 and 6 were chosen.
- **Line 5 (Felicia Ho):** `1/1/96` is only 6 characters, and `mmddyy8.` still reads it correctly.

---

## The `PROC PRINT` Step

```sas
PROC PRINT data = temp;
  title 'Output dataset: TEMP';
RUN;
```
This prints the dataset with a title. No `FORMAT` statement is given, so **`wt_date` is shown as the raw day count** rather than as a readable date:

```
Output dataset: TEMP

Obs  subj   f_name        l_name   height   wt_date   calorie
 1   1024   Alice         Smith      65      13118      2036
 2   1167   Maryann       White      68      13118      1800
 3   1168   Thomas        Jones       .      13119      2302
 4   1201   Benedictine   Arnold     68      13117      2432
 5   1302   Felicia       Ho         63      13149      1972
```

### Tip
To display the dates in readable form, add a format in the DATA step or in PROC PRINT:

```sas
format wt_date mmddyy10.;   /* shows 12/01/1995 */
```

To also show the thousands separator for calories, add:

```sas
format calorie comma5.;
```

# **Turn of the Dragon and the Fox**
*A Freedom Planet × Naruto × Civilization Crossover*

---

## **TURN 1 — 4000 BC**

The first thing Sash Lilac noticed was the silence.

No wind through Shang Tu's towers, no clatter of Carol's motorbike. Just grass, a slow river, and a strange hexagonal shimmer across the ground, like someone had laid an invisible honeycomb over the world.

The second thing she noticed was the blond boy face-down in the dirt beside her.

"Hey." She nudged his shoulder with her boot. "You alive?"

"Five more minutes, Iruka-sensei…" He rolled over, opened his eyes, and found a purple-haired dragon girl leaning over him, her twin tails swaying. He shot upright so fast he nearly headbutted her. "WHOA! Who are you?! Are you a summon? A tailed beast? Are you a *Sannin*?"

"I'm Lilac." She offered a hand and pulled him up. "I'm a dragon. Not a summon. I don't know what a Sannin is."

"Naruto Uzumaki! Future Hokage, dattebayo!" He grinned, then frowned at the sky. "Where's the village? Where's *anything*?"

Before Lilac could answer, a calm, ancient voice rolled across the plains like distant thunder:

> ***"Rise, leaders. Your people have wandered for generations. Now they look to you. Will you build an empire to stand the test of time?"***

Behind them stood two figures in rough hides. One carried a bundle of tools and a clay pot of embers. The other held a crude spear and saluted with grim seriousness.

Floating above their heads were glowing icons: a little **flag**, and a little **sword**.

"…Are they talking to *us*?" Naruto whispered.

"I think," Lilac said slowly, "we're in charge."

Naruto's face lit up like a festival lantern. "I'm a leader already?! I skipped straight to Hokage! WOOOO!"

The settler cleared his throat. A translucent panel unfolded in the air in front of Lilac:

> **SETTLER — Found City?**
> *Tile: Grassland, River, Coast-adjacent. Fresh Water: Yes.*

"River for water, ocean for trade, hills over there for defense." Lilac tapped her chin. "Back home, I'd kill for a spot like this."

"So we build here?"

"We build here."

She pressed the button.

The ground *rumbled*. Huts erupted from the earth, a palisade sketched itself into being, smoke curled from a central fire, and a banner unfurled bearing a symbol neither of them chose but both recognized: a **purple dragon coiled around an orange spiral**.

> **A new city has been founded!**
> **Name your capital:** `_________`

They looked at each other.

"Konoha," Naruto said instantly.
"Shang Tu," Lilac said at the exact same time.

A pause.

"…How about something new?" Lilac offered. "Since it's *ours*."

Naruto scratched his cheek. "Uh… *Spiral Peak*? 'Cause of the spiral and, y'know, dragons live on peaks?"

Lilac smiled. It was a better name than she expected. "Spiral Peak it is."

---

## **TURN 2 — 3960 BC**

> ***"Your people await your guidance. Choose a technology to research."***

A great glowing tree of ideas sprawled before them: Pottery, Animal Husbandry, Mining, Sailing, Archery, Astrology.

"Archery!" Naruto pointed. "Weapons! Defense!"

"Pottery," Lilac countered. "Granaries. Food. People can't fight if they're starving."

"Okay, but hear me out—what if we're starving *and* stabbed?"

She laughed despite herself. "Fine. We do Mining first. Tools help everyone, and it unlocks… oh, *Bronze Working* after."

"Bronze makes swords?"

"Bronze makes swords."

"Deal!"

Meanwhile, the city panel asked what to build. **Warrior**, **Builder**, **Settler**, **Monument**.

Naruto stared at "Builder" and got a dangerous look in his eye.

"Naruto, what are you—"

"**Shadow Clone Jutsu!**"

*POOF.* Eight Narutos appeared in a cloud of smoke, all striking poses.

The game *froze*. The city panel flickered. Somewhere far above reality, the ancient narrator voice hesitated:

> ***"…Unrecognized unit type."***

A clone picked up a shovel. Another started stacking stones. A third was already digging an irrigation ditch from the river with terrifying enthusiasm.

> ***"…Builders: +8. Charges: Until dispelled."***

Lilac stared, then burst out laughing so hard she had to sit down. "You just *broke the game*."

"I just made us a workforce!" Naruto beamed, chest puffed. "See? Leadership!"

"Okay, okay." Lilac wiped her eyes. "Then I'm doing my part too."

She took off running.

---

## **TURN 3 — 3920 BC**

Normally a warrior uncovers two tiles of fog per turn.

Lilac uncovered *forty*.

She tore across the plains in a purple streak, Dragon Boost blazing, the black fog of war peeling back around her like curtains. Forests. A mountain range to the north. A volcano steaming in the east. A natural wonder—an enormous crystal canyon that hummed when she ran past—

> **Natural Wonder Discovered: The Prism Gorge! (+Faith, +Science)**

—and on the edge of the coast, a cluster of red tents.

> ⚠️ **BARBARIAN OUTPOST SIGHTED**

She skidded to a stop on a hill, crouched low, and counted. A scout. Three spearmen. A campfire. And their scout had just spotted *her*.

"Oh, *that's* not good."

She raced home and came to a stop in Spiral Peak's square, kicking up dust. Naruto (the real one, eating something from a wooden bowl) looked up.

"Barbarians," she panted. "Southeast, by the coast. Their scout saw me. They're going to come looking for the city."

Naruto set the bowl down. All the goofiness drained from his face, replaced with something sharper.

"How many?"

"Three spearmen. Maybe more by next turn."

"Our one warrior guy can't handle that."

"No." Lilac glanced at the spear-holding warrior, who was nervously sweating. "But we're not exactly normal units."

Naruto grinned, slow and wide. "Yeah. We're *really* not."

She noticed the bowl. "What were you eating?"

"I tried to make ramen with river fish and wild wheat." He held it up. It was grey. "Turns out Pottery's kinda important."

"*Told* you."

"Yeah, yeah." He paused. Then, a bit quieter: "You ran all that way by yourself. You coulda gotten hurt."

Lilac blinked. Nobody back in Avalice really worried about her running off—it was just what she *did*. "I'm fast. I'm always fine."

"Still." He rubbed the back of his neck. "We're a team now, right? Spiral Peak's got two leaders. So… next time, take me with you."

Something warm flickered in her chest. She hid it behind a grin. "Can you keep up?"

"Believe it!"

---

## **TURN 4 — 3880 BC**

The barbarians came at dawn.

Five spearmen crested the hill—two more than Lilac counted—screaming war cries and banging spears against hide shields. The narrator voice intoned grimly:

> ***"Barbarians approach Spiral Peak! Defense strength: 8."***

The lone warrior gulped.

Then twenty Naruto clones dropped out of the trees.

"**Shadow Clone Jutsu! Uzumaki Barrage!**"

The clones swarmed like a wave of orange, tackling spearmen into the grass, yanking shields away, causing absolute chaos. The barbarians had absolutely no combat modifier for this.

One barbarian broke free and charged for the palisade gate.

A purple blur intercepted him.

"**Cyclone!**"

Lilac spun, hair-tails whipping into a hurricane, and launched the man clean over the river. He landed in the mud with a *splorp*, looked back at the city, and decided that this particular empire was *not* worth it.

The rest fled.

> **⚔️ Barbarian attack repelled!**
> **Combat Experience: +∞** *(error)*
> **Barbarian Outpost cleared: +50 Gold**

The townsfolk spilled out of their huts, cheering. Someone started drumming. Children ran circles around the clones, who poofed away one by one, until only the real Naruto was left standing beside Lilac in the trampled grass, both of them breathless and grinning.

"Not bad, dragon girl."

"Not bad yourself, *Hokage*."

He went pink to the ears. "You—you said it! You called me Hokage!"

"Well, you *are* a world leader now." She bumped his shoulder with hers. "It counts."

The sun set over Spiral Peak, painting the river gold. A new panel appeared quietly in the corner of their vision:

> **Technology Researched: Mining**
> **Now Researching: Pottery**

Naruto looked at it, then at her.

"You switched it."

Lilac shrugged, smiling up at the first stars. "Someone's gotta make real ramen in this world."

He didn't say anything for a moment. Then he sat down beside her on the hill, close enough that their shoulders touched, and they watched their tiny city glow beneath the darkening sky—two strangers from two different worlds, at the very beginning of history.

> ***"Turn 4 complete. 496 turns remain. Your legend has only begun."***

---

### **📜 Empire Summary — End of Turn 4**
| | |
|---|---|
| **Civilization** | The Spiral Dragon Alliance |
| **Leaders** | Sash Lilac & Naruto Uzumaki |
| **Capital** | Spiral Peak (Pop. 2) |
| **Units** | 1 Very Relieved Warrior, ∞ Shadow Clones (unstable) |
| **Gold** | 53 |
| **Wonders Found** | Prism Gorge |
| **Diplomatic Status** | Nobody's met them yet. *Gandhi is waiting.* |

---

*Want me to continue with **Turns 5–8**? (First contact with another civ, founding a second city, the Pottery-ramen breakthrough, and maybe a moonlit moment by the Prism Gorge…)* 🐉🍥

# Line-by-Line Explanation of the SAS INPUT Code

This DATA step reads fixed-format raw data using **column pointer controls** (`@n` and `+n`) and **informats** (e.g., `4.`, `$11.`, `mmddyy8.`). Each variable is read from an exact location on the data line.

## Column Layout of the Data

It helps to see where each field sits on a data line:

```
Column:  1   5   10   15   20   25   30   35   40   45
         |---|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|--
         1201 Benedictine Arnold 2 68 190 11/30/95 2,432
         └──┘ └─────────┘ └────┘ │ └┘ └─┘ └──────┘ └───┘
         subj   f_name    l_name │ ht  wt   date    cal
         1-4    6-16      18-23  │27-28 30-32 34-41  43-47
                               gender(25)
```

## The DATA Statement

```sas
DATA temp;
```
This starts a DATA step and creates a temporary dataset named `TEMP`, stored in the `WORK` library. It is deleted when the SAS session ends.

## The INPUT Statement

### Line 1: `input @1 subj 4.`
- `@1` is an **absolute pointer control**. It moves the input pointer to column 1.
- `subj` is the variable name. It is numeric because there is no `$`.
- `4.` is a numeric informat that reads 4 columns, here columns 1–4.
- Result: `subj = 1024`, `1167`, and so on.
- After reading, the pointer sits at column 5.

### Line 2: `@6 f_name $11.`
- `@6` moves the pointer to column 6.
- `$11.` is a character informat that reads 11 columns, here columns 6–16.
- The width of 11 is chosen to fit the longest first name, "Benedictine", which has exactly 11 characters. Shorter names such as "Alice" are padded with trailing blanks.
- After reading, the pointer is at column 17.

### Line 3: `@18 l_name $6.`
- `@18` moves the pointer to column 18. Column 17 is the blank separator, and it is skipped.
- `$6.` reads 6 characters, here columns 18–23. This fits "Arnold", the longest last name.
- After reading, the pointer is at column 24.

### Line 4: `+3 height 2.`
- `+3` is a **relative pointer control**. It moves the pointer 3 columns forward from its current position, so from column 24 to column 27.
- This skips columns 24–26, which contain a blank, the **gender code** (1 or 2) in column 25, and another blank. As a result, **the gender value is never read**.
- `2.` reads 2 numeric columns, here columns 27–28.
- Result: `height = 65`, `68`, and so on.
- For Thomas Jones, columns 27–28 are blank, so `height` is set to **missing** (`.`).
- After reading, the pointer is at column 29.

### Line 5: `+5 wt_date mmddyy8.`
- `+5` moves the pointer from column 29 to column 34.
- This skips columns 29–33, which contain the **weight** values (125, 140, 190, …) in columns 30–32. As a result, **weight is not read either**.
- `mmddyy8.` is a **date informat**. It reads up to 8 columns, here columns 34–41, in month/day/year form.
- It handles varying formats such as `12/1/95`, `12/01/95`, and `1/1/96`. Trailing blanks inside the 8-column field are fine.
- The value is stored as a **SAS date value**, which is the number of days since January 1, 1960.
- After reading, the pointer is at column 42.

### Line 6: `+1 calorie comma5.;`
- `+1` moves the pointer from column 42 to column 43.
- `comma5.` reads 5 columns, here columns 43–47. It **removes embedded commas** (and also `$`, `%`, blanks, and parentheses) before converting the text to a number.
- Result: `"2,036"` becomes `2036`.
- The semicolon ends the INPUT statement.

## The DATALINES Section

```sas
DATALINES;
...
  ;
```
- `DATALINES;` tells SAS that the raw data follows directly in the program.
- The lone `;` on its own line marks the end of the data. Leading spaces before it are fine.
- `RUN;` executes the DATA step.

## Summary of What Is Read and What Is Skipped

| Columns | Content | Variable | Informat |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–4 | Subject ID | `subj` | `4.` |
| 6–16 | First name | `f_name` | `$11.` |
| 18–23 | Last name | `l_name` | `$6.` |
| 25 | Gender | *skipped* | — |
| 27–28 | Height | `height` | `2.` |
| 30–32 | Weight | *skipped* | — |
| 34–41 | Weigh-in date | `wt_date` | `mmddyy8.` |
| 43–47 | Calories | `calorie` | `comma5.` |

## PROC PRINT Output

```sas
PROC PRINT data = temp;
  title 'Output dataset: TEMP';
RUN;
```

This prints the dataset. Because no `FORMAT` statement was applied, `wt_date` appears as raw day counts:

```
                    Output dataset: TEMP

Obs    subj    f_name         l_name    height    wt_date    calorie
 1     1024    Alice          Smith       65       13118      2036
 2     1167    Maryann        White       68       13118      1800
 3     1168    Thomas         Jones        .       13119      2302
 4     1201    Benedictine    Arnold      68       13117      2432
 5     1302    Felicia        Ho          63       13149      1972
```

## Tip

To display readable dates and commas in the output, add a FORMAT statement in the DATA step or in PROC PRINT:

```sas
format wt_date mmddyy10. calorie comma5.;
```

With that statement, `13118` displays as `12/01/1995`, and `2036` displays as `2,036`.

- `DATALINES;` signals that the raw data follows directly in the program (in-stream data).

## Chrome Extension File Types

- **`.crx`**: the packaged extension format, used for distribution. It is a signed ZIP archive with an extra header.
- **Unpacked folder**: after installation, Chrome extracts the `.crx` into a regular folder. Inside you'll find:
  - `manifest.json` (required; describes the extension)
  - `.js` (scripts), `.html`, `.css`
  - `.png` / `.svg` (icons)
  - `_locales/` (translations), `_metadata/` (signature/verification data)

## Where They're Stored

Each extension sits in a folder named by its **32-letter extension ID**, with a version subfolder:
`Extensions/<extension-id>/<version>/`

### macOS (your system)
```
~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Extensions/
```
For other profiles, replace `Default` with `Profile 1`, `Profile 2`, etc.

### Windows
```
%LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Extensions\
```
(usually `C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Extensions\`)

### Linux
```
~/.config/google-chrome/Default/Extensions/
```

## Tips
- **Find an extension's ID**: open `chrome://extensions`, turn on **Developer mode** (top right), and the ID appears under each extension.
- **Find your profile path**: open `chrome://version` and look at **Profile Path**.
- On macOS, `~/Library` is hidden by default. In Finder press **Cmd+Shift+G** and paste the path, or run:
  ```bash
  open ~/Library/Application\ Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Extensions/
  ```
- Extension settings and data are stored separately, in `Local Extension Settings/` and `IndexedDB/` in the same profile folder.

turns.content: As an industrial giant, GM has a yearly business turnover of $180 billion. Do you think being “big” helps in the highly competitive automotive world?

# Does Being "Big" Help GM?

**Yes, but size is an advantage only when it's well managed.** Scale gives GM real competitive weapons, and it also creates serious liabilities. GM's own history shows both.

## Where Size Helps

**1. Economies of scale**
- Fixed costs such as R&D, tooling, platforms, and marketing are spread over millions of vehicles, which lowers the cost per unit.
- Global platforms (for example, the BEV3/Ultium architecture) let one engineering investment support many models across Chevrolet, GMC, Cadillac, and Buick.

**2. Purchasing power**
- GM buys enormous volumes of steel, chips, and battery materials, so it can negotiate better prices and get priority during shortages, as seen in the 2021–22 semiconductor crisis.

**3. Capacity to fund huge bets**
- The shift to EVs, software, and autonomy needs tens of billions of dollars. GM has committed heavily to battery plants (Ultium Cells with LG) and, until recently, to Cruise. Smaller automakers simply can't take bets of that size.

**4. Brand portfolio and market coverage**
- GM spans segments from affordable cars to luxury models, and from pickups to commercial vans (BrightDrop). Strong profits from trucks and SUVs fund newer ventures.

**5. Distribution and service network**
- Thousands of dealers and a broad parts network create a barrier that new entrants struggle to replicate.

**6. Influence and resilience**
- Large firms have leverage with governments, suppliers, and unions, and can absorb shocks better than smaller rivals.

## Where Size Hurts

**1. Bureaucracy and slow decisions**
- Layers of management can delay product launches and dull responsiveness. Tesla and Chinese EV makers such as BYD iterate much faster.

**2. Legacy costs**
- Pension and healthcare obligations, union contracts, and an aging plant footprint were central to GM's **2009 bankruptcy**. Being big did not prevent failure, and it arguably made the fall harder.

**3. Brand dilution and complexity**
- At its peak GM had too many overlapping brands (Pontiac, Saturn, Hummer, Saab, Oldsmobile), which cannibalized each other and wasted resources.

**4. Innovator's dilemma**
- Profitable gas-powered trucks create an incentive to protect the existing business rather than disrupt it. GM's EV1 in the 1990s is a famous example of a lead that was abandoned.

**5. Big bets, big losses**
- Scale magnifies mistakes. GM poured billions into Cruise before pulling back on robotaxis, and it has had to slow EV production plans as demand softened.

## The Competitive Reality

| Factor | Advantage to big incumbents | Advantage to agile challengers |
|---|---|---|
| Manufacturing cost | ✅ | |
| Capital access | ✅ | |
| Software and speed | | ✅ |
| Brand trust and dealers | ✅ | |
| Freedom from legacy costs | | ✅ |
| Vertical integration in EVs | Mixed | ✅ (BYD, Tesla) |

Tellingly, **Toyota sells more vehicles than GM with greater efficiency**, and **Tesla has at times been worth far more** despite much lower revenue. So revenue size alone doesn't determine competitive strength.

## Conclusion

Being big is a **necessary but not sufficient** condition for success in the auto industry. Scale is almost essential now, given the capital demands of electrification, software, and global supply chains, and smaller independent automakers have largely disappeared or merged (for example, Stellantis). However, size becomes an advantage only when combined with:
- **Focus**: fewer, stronger brands (GM's post-2009 restructuring)
- **Agility**: faster decisions and software-driven development
- **Disciplined capital allocation**: knowing when to double down and when to cut losses

GM after 2009, leaner and more focused, shows how to make size work for you. GM before 2009 shows how size can become a burden.

# Does Being "Big" Help GM?

**Yes, but only conditionally.** Size gives GM real advantages, but size alone doesn't win. What matters is whether the company turns size into *useful scale* and stays agile enough to act on it.

## Where Size Helps

**1. Economies of scale**
Cars have huge fixed costs: plants, tooling, engineering, and crash testing. Spreading those across millions of vehicles a year lowers unit costs. GM can share platforms and components across Chevrolet, GMC, Buick, and Cadillac.

**2. Purchasing power**
As one of the largest buyers of steel, semiconductors, and battery materials, GM can negotiate better prices and get priority during shortages, such as the 2021–22 chip crisis.

**3. R&D and capital for big bets**
EVs, battery chemistry, software, and autonomy need billions in upfront investment. GM could fund the Ultium battery platform, joint-venture battery plants, and years of Cruise development. Few smaller companies could absorb those costs.

**4. Distribution and brand reach**
A large dealer and service network, fleet relationships, and strong brands (especially in trucks and SUVs) create barriers that newcomers struggle to match.

**5. Resilience and influence**
A big balance sheet helps a company survive downturns, and size brings political leverage over trade, tariffs, and subsidies.

## Where Size Hurts

**1. Bureaucracy and slow decisions**
Large hierarchies move slowly. Tesla and BYD have iterated faster on EVs and software than legacy giants.

**2. Legacy costs and rigidity**
Big incumbents carry pension obligations, union contracts, aging plants, and franchise dealer laws. These burdens contributed to GM's 2009 bankruptcy.

**3. Complexity and diluted focus**
Too many brands, markets, and models spread resources thin. GM has improved partly by *shrinking*: it sold Opel/Vauxhall (2017), retired Holden, exited India and other markets, and shut down Cruise's robotaxi business (2024).

**4. Innovator's dilemma**
Profitable gasoline trucks fund the company but can make it reluctant to cannibalize itself with riskier technology.

## The Key Insight: Size ≠ Scale

- **Toyota** is huge *and* efficient, thanks to lean manufacturing, disciplined platforms, and a long-term strategy.
- **Tesla** has had far lower volumes than GM but at times a much higher market value, because of its software, its vertical integration, and investor belief in its growth.
- **BYD** combines massive scale with vertical integration (it makes its own batteries and chips), giving it a cost edge that size alone wouldn't.

## Conclusion

Being big is a **necessary but not sufficient** condition for success in the auto industry. It provides the money, purchasing power, and staying power to compete through a costly transition to EVs and software-defined vehicles. But revenue of $180 billion is only an advantage if GM:
- keeps its portfolio focused,
- shares platforms aggressively to lower costs,
- moves quickly on software and batteries, and
- avoids the bureaucratic inertia that nearly sank it in 2009.

In short, **size gives GM the ability to compete, but how well it competes depends on its strategy and agility.**

# Does Being "Big" Help GM?

**Size is a real advantage in the auto industry, but only when it's paired with agility and focus. On its own it can become a liability.** GM's history shows both sides.

## How Size Helps

**1. Economies of scale**
Automaking is capital-intensive. A new vehicle platform can cost $1–6 billion to develop. GM spreads these costs across millions of vehicles, lowering per-unit costs. Shared platforms (e.g., trucks and SUVs across Chevrolet, GMC, and Cadillac) multiply this benefit.

**2. Purchasing power**
As one of the world's largest buyers of steel, semiconductors, and components, GM can negotiate better prices and priority supply. This mattered during the 2021–22 chip shortage.

**3. Funding the future**
The shift to EVs, software-defined vehicles, and autonomy requires tens of billions in investment. GM's scale let it commit roughly $35 billion to EVs and AVs and build Ultium battery plants with LG. Smaller players struggle to fund such transitions alone.

**4. Brand portfolio and market coverage**
Multiple brands let GM serve different segments and price points, spreading risk across markets.

**5. Distribution and service network**
Thousands of dealerships provide sales reach, after-sales service, and customer trust that new entrants take decades to build.

**6. Financial muscle**
GM Financial supports sales through loans and leases. A large balance sheet helps the company survive downturns.

**7. Influence**
Size brings bargaining power with governments, unions, and partners, which helps with regulations, subsidies, and trade policy.

## How Size Can Hurt

**1. Bureaucracy and slow decisions**
Large hierarchies can delay responses to market shifts. GM was slow to react to fuel-efficient Japanese imports in the 1970s–80s and later to Tesla's EV push.

**2. Legacy costs**
Pension obligations, healthcare liabilities, union contracts, and excess plant capacity weighed heavily on GM. Combined with the 2008 financial crisis, they led to the 2009 bankruptcy and government bailout. Being big did not save GM; it arguably made the fall bigger.

**3. Complexity and brand dilution**
At its peak, GM had too many overlapping brands (Pontiac, Saturn, Oldsmobile, Hummer, Saab), which cannibalized each other. Shedding them improved focus.

**4. Innovation disadvantage**
Smaller, focused competitors can move faster. Tesla and BYD outpaced incumbents in EVs and software. GM's own robotaxi unit, Cruise, was shut down in late 2024 after heavy spending, a reminder that money does not guarantee success.

**5. Global retreat**
GM exited Europe (selling Opel/Vauxhall in 2017) and scaled back in India, Australia, and other markets. This shows that size without regional competitiveness isn't sustainable.

## Conclusion

Being big gives GM **resources, resilience, and reach** that are essential in an industry with huge fixed costs and a costly technological transition. But size is **necessary, not sufficient**. The post-2009 GM has done better by becoming *leaner*: fewer brands, a focus on profitable trucks and SUVs, and selective bets on EVs.

The lesson is that being big helps most when a company **uses its scale strategically while staying agile enough to adapt.** In today's automotive world, the main threat comes less from bigger rivals and more from faster ones.

# Set Pitch: **"Lockkeeper's Rise"**
### Theme: **CANALWICK**, a town that runs on water

---

## The Theme in One Line
A sprawling, hand-cranked canal town where every bridge lifts, every lock floods, and every delivery arrives by narrowboat. **CANALWICK** turns working waterway engineering into cozy, mechanical, story-driven play.

## Why This Theme
- **A white space in the market.** Most construction-toy ranges cover cities, space, fantasy castles or licensed media. Few explore **gentle mechanical systems** that kids can see working.
- **Built-in modularity.** Canals connect naturally. Every set adds a stretch of waterway, so the town grows in a line, a loop or a grid.
- **Appeal across ages.** Kids get boats, cranks and characters. Adults get a cozy, intricate display piece with real engineering logic.
- **Original world.** Canalwick is a fictional market town of narrow brick warehouses, painted boats, rope-and-pulley cranes and a slightly eccentric guild of Lockkeepers who keep the water moving.

---

## The Set: **#71204 Lockkeeper's Rise**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pieces** | ~1,150 |
| **Age** | 9+ |
| **Price tier** | Upper mid-range (flagship of Wave 1) |
| **Figures** | 5 + 1 animal |
| **Footprint** | ~38 × 26 cm, two canal levels |

### The Hook
A **fully working two-stage canal lock**. Turn the paddle-gear crank, and stacked transparent-blue "water tiles" rise on a hidden scissor lift, carrying a narrowboat from the lower canal up to the upper basin. Open the gates, and the boat sails into town.

---

## The Build

**1. The Lower Basin (bag 1–3)**
A cobbled towpath, a mooring post, a small fuel-and-rope store and the lower lock gates. The kid builds the narrowboat first, so the play starts early.

**2. The Lock Chamber (bag 4–7)**
The mechanical heart. The scissor-lift mechanism sits under a stone-textured chamber, and the "water surface" is a rigid plate of trans-blue tiles that rises about 6 studs. A side-mounted ratchet crank with an audible click-stop holds the water level in place.

**3. The Lockkeeper's Cottage (bag 8–10)**
A narrow, three-storey brick-and-timber house perched beside the lock:
- **Ground floor:** gear room with visible cogs (a window shows the mechanism moving)
- **Middle floor:** kitchen with stove and tide-tables pinned to the wall
- **Top floor:** lookout with a signal lamp and a telescope
- **Roof:** pigeon loft (the town's "mail system")

**4. The Upper Basin & Swing Bridge (bag 11–12)**
A pivoting footbridge that swings aside when a boat passes, plus a small hand crane for unloading cargo crates.

---

## Play Features
1. **Rising lock.** Crank to lift a boat between levels (the signature feature).
2. **Swinging gates.** Lock gates on both ends open with balance-beam levers, as on real canals.
3. **Swing bridge.** Pivots 90° to let boats through.
4. **Cargo crane.** A string winch lifts crates from boat to quay.
5. **Signal lamp.** A rotating red/green disc tells boats when to wait or go.
6. **Detachable narrowboat.** It floats in a real bath and has a removable roof showing a tiny cabin interior.
7. **Pigeon post.** A hidden compartment holds a printed "message" tile tied to the theme's story.

---

## Characters
- **Marrow Thimble**, the elderly Lockkeeper. Gruff, kind, and has never missed a tide in 40 years. Exclusive to this set.
- **Pip Thimble**, Marrow's grandchild and Lockkeeper-in-training, with an oversized wrench accessory.
- **Odessa Vane**, captain of the narrowboat *Kettle Lark*. She delivers tea, coal and gossip.
- **Brann**, a dockhand with a cargo hook and flat cap.
- **The Inspector**, a mysterious Canal Board official with a clipboard. Is he here to help, or to shut the lock down?
- **Nettle**, the lock cat (animal figure).

**Story hook:** The Canal Board wants to replace Canalwick's old locks with a modern pumping station. Marrow and Pip must prove the old ways still work. This thread runs across the whole wave.

---

## Modularity & Range Connection
- **Standard "Canal Connector" edges.** Every Canalwick set ends in a uniform 16-stud-wide water channel with a clip joint, so any set links to any other.
- **Level system.** Locks connect "Low Canal" and "High Canal" sets, so this flagship is the bridge between two tiers of the range.
- **Wave 1 siblings** (smaller, cheaper entry points):
  - *Tea Barge Delivery* (~250 pcs): a boat plus a floating dock
  - *Ropewalk Warehouse* (~600 pcs): a tall storehouse with a pulley hoist
  - *Canal Board Pump House* (~800 pcs): the "rival" set, with a menacing steam pump
  - *Towpath Horse & Cart* (~120 pcs): an impulse-buy set with a horse figure

---

## Selling Points
- **Visible mechanics teach real engineering**: gears, ratchets, levers, counterweights and how locks really work. A printed insert in the instructions explains the real-world principle.
- **A cozy aesthetic** that suits the current adult-fan market (warm brick reds, painted boat liveries, lanterns).
- **Screen-free storytelling** through the pigeon-post messages, which build a narrative across sets.
- **Strong shelf presence.** The tiered build and rising boat make it a natural display piece and an eye-catching hero image for the box.

## Packaging Concept
The box front shows the boat mid-lift at dusk, with lamps lit and Nettle the cat watching from the cottage window. The back shows a panoramic "map" of all Wave 1 sets connected into one canal street.

## Risks & Mitigations
| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Lift mechanism fragility | Use a ratchet lock to prevent slipping, and test the mechanism with kids |
| Theme seen as "quiet" vs. action lines | Inspector/Pump House rivalry adds stakes and conflict |
| Large footprint | Lock module detaches cleanly for smaller-shelf display |

---

**Tagline:** *"Raise the water. Open the gates. Keep Canalwick moving."*

# Theme Pitch: **TIDEMARK**
*A city that lives by the tide*

## The Theme in One Line
Halvenmoor is a canal-city on a vast tidal estuary. Twice a day the sea floods in and the streets become waterways. Twice a day it drains away and the canals become markets. Everything in Halvenmoor is built to **transform between Low Water and High Water**.

## Why This Theme
- **Built-in transformation.** Every set has two states, which doubles the play value without doubling the parts.
- **Original world.** It draws on no existing IP and no existing toy line. It's a fresh, ownable setting.
- **Both kinds of fan.** Kids get boats, chases, and transforming builds. Adult builders get dense, characterful town architecture.
- **Collectible logic.** The sets physically link to form a growing tidal district.

---

## The Set: **The Lockkeeper's Swing Bridge**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Set number** | TM-31042 |
| **Pieces** | ~860 |
| **Age** | 9+ |
| **Target RRP** | £79.99 / $89.99 / €89.99 |
| **Footprint** | 32×48 stud base, with canal-edge connectors on both short sides |
| **Figures** | 5 |

### The Pitch
At the heart of every Halvenmoor district stands a lockkeeper's tower. It controls the swing bridge, the sluice gate, and the great tide bell that warns the city the sea is coming. This set captures the busiest corner of the canal network in the moment between Low Water and High Water.

### The Build

**1. The Lockkeeper's Tower (3 storeys)**
- **Ground floor:** a sluice control room with a large brick-built gear wheel.
- **First floor:** the lockkeeper's cluttered living quarters, with a stove, a hammock, a tide-chart wall, and a cat.
- **Top floor:** an open belfry holding the **Tide Bell**. It rings with a satisfying clunk when you turn a crank on the side.
- **Rooftop:** a weathervane shaped like a leaping eel.

**2. The Swing Bridge**
A cobbled footbridge spans the canal and rotates 90° on a turntable at the tower's base. Turning the tower's main gear wheel swings the bridge open to let tall-masted boats through.

**3. The Sluice Gate**
A sliding gate in the canal raises and lowers on a rack-and-pinion. It can trap a boat, or a fleeing smuggler.

**4. The Canal Bed**
The canal bed is a recessed channel in the base. It's tiled in printed "wet cobble" at the bottom so it reads as a dry street at Low Water.

### ⭐ Signature Feature: The Tide Switch
A lever on the base edge flips the whole set between modes.

| | **Low Water** | **High Water** |
|---|---|---|
| **Canal surface** | Hinged translucent-blue "water panels" are tucked vertically against the canal walls, exposing the dry cobbled canal bed | The panels fold down flat over the channel, creating the canal surface |
| **Canal bed** | A market street: a fish stall clips onto the canal bed, and a handcart rolls along it | The boat docks clip onto the water's surface |
| **Tower** | Ground-floor doors open onto the street | Flood boards slide up to seal the ground floor |
| **Barge** | Sits on its keel stand as a market stall | Floats in the canal |

It's simple, robust, and needs no special elements: just hinges, clips, and tiles. It gives the set a clear "wow" moment for the box art and the advert.

### Included Vehicle: The Mudlark Barge
- A small flat-bottomed cargo barge with a folding mast, so it fits under the bridge when the bridge is closed.
- Removable cargo crates (one hides a smuggled glowing "sea-pearl").
- Its keel converts into a stand, so it doubles as a market stall at Low Water.

### The Figures
1. **Orla Fenwick, the Lockkeeper.** She's weathered, wears oilskins and a brass whistle, and is never late with the bell. *Hero figure.*
2. **Pim, her apprentice.** An eager kid with oversized waders and a satchel of tide charts.
3. **"Gullet" Marsh, the smuggler.** A barge captain with a double-sided face (charming / caught out).
4. **Saffi Okonkwo, the fishmonger.** She runs the Low Water market stall.
5. **The Constable of the Tidewatch.** City law enforcement on canal patrol, with a boathook.

**Plus:** Bramble, the lockkeeper's cat (a creature element), and three eels.

---

## Play Scenarios Built Into the Box
- **"Race the Tide."** Gullet must get his barge through the lock before the bell rings and Orla closes the sluice.
- **"Market Day."** Low Water mode becomes a bustling street scene, until the bell rings and everyone scrambles.
- **"Who Stole the Sea-Pearl?"** A light mystery. Clues are hidden in the tower via printed tiles: a footprint, a torn map, and a wet coin.

---

## How It Fits the Wider Range
Every Tidemark set has standardised **canal-edge connectors**, so the canals of different sets join up into one continuous waterway. Each set's Tide Switch works independently, and a later "Tidemill" set could add a mechanism that triggers neighbouring sets in sequence.

| Wave | Set | Price tier | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wave 1 | Tidewatch Patrol Skiff | Entry | Impulse buy |
| Wave 1 | Eel-Catcher's Hut | Small | Builds the cast |
| Wave 1 | **The Lockkeeper's Swing Bridge** | Mid | **Flagship hero set** |
| Wave 1 | The Drowned Market Hall | Large | Display piece |
| Wave 2 | The Smuggler's Undercroft | | Villain lair beneath the streets |
| Wave 2 | The Great Tidemill | | Motorised range-expander |

**Expanded universe hooks:** the mysterious sea-pearls, the abandoned "Sunken Quarter" that only emerges at the lowest spring tides, and the rumour of something enormous that moves in the deep estuary channel.

---

## Marketing Hook
**Tagline:** *"Twice a day, everything changes."*

**Box art:** A split image. The left half shows the set at Low Water in warm daylight, with the market busy. The right half shows the same set at High Water at dusk, with lanterns lit, the bridge swung open, and the barge slipping through. A diagonal wave-line divides the two halves.

**Adult-fan angle:** The tower uses the range's standard modular-building connector points, so it can sit alongside traditional town streetscapes. The canal-city architecture, with its stepped gables, timber jetties, and tide-stained brick (a printed waterline gradient), gives display builders something new.

# NIGHTPOST: The Lantern Couriers of Hollowmere

## Theme Overview

**Premise:** In the drowsy valley town of Hollowmere, nothing important happens by day. Everyone sleeps through the sunlight, and the real work begins at dusk. The **Nightpost** is a guild of lantern-carrying couriers who deliver letters, parcels and the occasional runaway dream across rooftops, chimney-stacks and fog-filled ravines. They work alongside giant, gentle **lantern moths**, which are drawn to the couriers' glowing satchels and carry them through the dark.

Their problem is **the Muddle**, a mischievous, shapeless fog-creature that drifts in from the marshes. It scrambles addresses, swaps parcels and hides letters in the wrong chimneys. It isn't evil. It just loves confusion.

**Theme pillars:**
- **Cosy nocturnal adventure.** Warm lamplight against deep indigo, with a storybook rather than action-movie tone.
- **Sorting and delivery play.** A real loop: collect, sort, deliver, foil the Muddle.
- **Glow as a mechanic.** Glow-in-the-dark elements are central to play, not decoration.

**Palette:** Midnight blue, slate grey, brass/pearl gold, warm amber transparent, and a signature dusty lilac for the moths.

---

## Flagship Set: **The Gloamwing Sorting Barge**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Age** | 8+ |
| **Element count** | ~740 |
| **Price tier** | Upper-mid (roughly the "large playset" bracket) |
| **Build size** | ~38 cm long × 22 cm tall × 14 cm wide |
| **Figures** | 4 figures + 2 brick-built creatures |

### The Model

The Gloamwing is a flying post-office barge. It is a stout, round-bellied wooden hull slung beneath a patched canvas gasbag and towed through the night sky by a giant lantern moth. It is the Nightpost's mobile sorting office, drifting over Hollowmere and dropping mail down chimneys as it passes.

**Build sections:**
1. **The Hull.** A chunky boat shape with curved brown elements and brass trim. It hinges open along one side to reveal a two-level interior.
2. **The Sorting Deck (interior).**
   - A **rotating sorting wheel** with six pigeonhole slots, turned by a crank at the stern.
   - A tiny stamping desk, a kettle on a stove, and a hammock for the off-shift courier.
   - A trapdoor in the floor with a **pulley-and-string parcel drop** that lowers a weighted mailbag on a cord.
3. **The Gasbag.** Sail-fabric or flexible-element balloon held by a brick-built rigging frame. A **swinging lantern** hangs at the bow.
4. **Mothra-sized companion: "Old Velvet."** A large brick-built lantern moth (~20 cm wingspan) with posable ball-joint wings. Its wing panels use **glow-in-the-dark printed elements**. It attaches to the barge by tow-lines, or can be detached and flown separately with a saddle for one figure.

### Figures

- **Postmistress Ada Thimble.** The barge's captain. Brass spectacles, oversized mail cap, and a figure-scale lantern accessory that glows.
- **Pim Ashgrove.** A young apprentice courier on his first night shift. Satchel accessory, startled/grinning dual-print face.
- **Corporal Fennick.** A retired night-watchman who now works as the barge's engineer. Wrench, moustache, grumpy/laughing dual face.
- **Mrs. Oddby.** A sleepy townsperson in nightcap and slippers, waiting at her chimney for a long-overdue parcel. Comes with a small brick-built rooftop-and-chimney diorama.

**Creatures:**
- **Old Velvet** (lantern moth, described above).
- **A Muddle-wisp.** A small brick-built fog creature made of clustered transparent-clear and trans-white elements, with two printed mischievous eyes. It clips onto any stud so it can "possess" a letter slot or chimney.

### Signature Play Features

1. **Collectible Letter Tiles.** The set includes 12 printed 1×2 "envelope" tiles. Each shows an address glyph (Bakery, Clocktower, Bridge House, Mrs. Oddby, etc.). Children sort them into matching slots on the sorting wheel, then "deliver" them via the parcel drop.
   - *Range hook:* every other Nightpost set contains a building or location whose glyph matches one of these tiles. The barge "delivers" to the whole range.

2. **The Muddle Mechanic.** The sorting wheel has a hidden spring-flip panel. Press a lever and the Muddle-wisp pops out of a pigeonhole, scattering the letters. The kids then have to re-sort them.

3. **Lights Out Mode.** Turn off the bedroom lights and the moth's wings, the lantern, and certain chimney-top "Delivered!" stars glow. It's designed for bedtime play and fits the theme's cosy night tone. Glow elements are deliberately placed to *show where deliveries have been made*.

4. **Detachable Flight.** Unhook Old Velvet for solo swooshing adventures with Pim aboard. Re-hook the tow lines to reunite the barge.

### Packaging & Instructions

- **Box art:** The barge drifting over a moonlit sea of rooftops, with Old Velvet's glowing wings lighting the clouds and the Muddle peeking from a chimney below. The box has a "glow-preview" spot-varnish window.
- **Instructions** are framed as a **courier's logbook**. Build steps are interspersed with short comic panels following Pim's first night on the job. The book ends with a **printed delivery map** of Hollowmere for tile-sorting games.

### Range Fit

The Gloamwing is the wave's hero set. Supporting sets might include:
- **Moth Stable Rooftop** (small entry set, ~150 pieces)
- **Clocktower Post Office** (large modular building)
- **The Muddle's Marsh Lair** (fog creature build-a-beast with "lost letter" hoard)
- **Night Courier Velocipede** (impulse-price vehicle)

Each contains letter tiles and an address glyph, so collecting the range expands the sorting game.

---

**Elevator pitch:**
*"Nightpost is a cosy, glow-in-the-dark world of moth-riding couriers who deliver the mail while the town sleeps. It's built for bedtime play, collectible sorting games, and a mischievous fog-creature who keeps getting everything wrong."*

Translate to Middle French

""Oh, they're over there, talking to Mary and Beldegar.""

« Ho ! ilz sont illec, qui parlent a Marie et a Beldegar. »

**Notes:**
- **Ho !** is a common Middle French interjection. *Ha !* also works.
- **ilz**: Middle French usually spelled the masculine plural pronoun with a *-z*.
- **illec** means "there, in that place." You could also use *la* or *par dela*.
- **qui parlent a…** ("who are speaking to…") was a natural way to express an ongoing action. A participial alternative is *parlans a Marie et a Beldegar*, where the participle could still take a plural *-s*.
- **a Marie et a Beldegar**: the preposition *a* is repeated before each name, as was typical. Accents like *à* were not yet in regular use.

turns.content: Sash Lilac & Naruto Uzumaki got into the world Sid Meier’s Civilization. year/Move 1-4 (Lilac x Naruto)

# **Civilization: Dragon & Ninja**
### *Turns 1–4*

---

## **TURN 1 — 4000 BC**

The first thing Sash Lilac noticed was the grid.

Not a literal one. But the ground under her boots felt *sectioned*, like the world had been cut into neat hexagonal tiles. The grassland she stood on ended in a sharp line, and past it was a plains tile, then a river, then a hill with a single deer standing perfectly still as if it were waiting to be counted.

"Okay," Lilac said slowly, tail flicking. "That's new."

"HEY! Is anyone else seeing *floating words?!*"

She spun around. A blond boy in an orange jumpsuit was jabbing a finger at the sky, where glowing text hung in the air:

> **CHOOSE YOUR LEADER. FOUND YOUR CIVILIZATION. STAND THE TEST OF TIME.**

"Floating words," Lilac confirmed. "Also a deer that hasn't blinked in two minutes."

The boy turned and his eyes went wide. "Whoa. You're a dragon? Like a *real* one?"

"Water dragon. Well, mostly. It's complicated." She held out a hand. "Sash Lilac."

He grinned and shook it hard. "Naruto Uzumaki! Future Hokage! ...Uh, wherever *here* is."

Behind them stood a small group of people in rough tunics, holding tents and bundles of grain. Above their heads hung a tiny banner shaped like a covered wagon. They were staring at the two of them.

"I think," Lilac said, "those are *ours.*"

One of the settlers stepped forward. "Great leaders! Where shall we found our capital?"

Naruto's grin got bigger. "Right here! Believe it!"

"Wait, wait!" Lilac grabbed his sleeve. "Think about it first. We're on grassland next to a river. River means fresh water. That hill over there has a deer, so that's food. And look, that tile's shiny."

Naruto squinted. "...That rock is sparkling."

"Resources! It's probably something valuable." She gave him a confident smile. "Settling on the river is the smart move."

Naruto rubbed the back of his head. "You sound like Shikamaru. Except less lazy."

"I'll take that as a compliment."

"It was one!"

The settlers planted a stake in the riverbank. The ground *shimmered*, walls rose out of the earth, and a banner unfurled above the new city. The text above them changed:

> **NAME YOUR CAPITAL.**

They both answered at the same moment.

"Shang Leaf!"

They looked at each other.

"...Shang Tu and the Hidden Leaf," Lilac said, laughing. "Okay, that's kind of perfect."

Naruto's cheeks went a little pink. "Heh. Great minds, right?"

> **SHANG LEAF has been founded. Population: 1.**

---

## **TURN 2 — 3960 BC**

"Forty years passed," Lilac said flatly, "and *nobody* aged."

"Is that how time works here?" Naruto was sitting on the city wall, legs swinging. "Because I'm not complaining."

A glowing menu hovered in front of them, labeled **RESEARCH**.

"Okay, technologies," Lilac said, scrolling with one claw. "Pottery, Animal Husbandry, Mining, Archery—"

"ARCHERY. Wait, no. Is there one for *ninja?*"

"I don't see 'Ninja' in the Ancient Era."

"Lame."

"Mining would let us work that sparkly rock," Lilac said, tapping her chin. "But Animal Husbandry shows us horses, and we might want speed later." She smiled a little to herself. "I like speed."

Naruto leaned over her shoulder to look, close enough that she caught the smell of ramen broth and campfire smoke. She ignored the small flutter in her chest. *Focus, Lilac. Running a civilization here.*

"Your call," Naruto said. "You're the strategy person. I'll be the 'punch whatever shows up' person."

"That's not a real role."

"It's *totally* a real role."

She picked **Mining**. Then the production menu opened.

> **SHANG LEAF is producing: ???**

"Scout," Lilac said at once. "We need to know what's around us."

"Or," Naruto said, raising a finger, "I could just..."

He crossed his fingers into a seal. "**Shadow Clone Jutsu!**"

*POOF.*

Three Narutos landed on the grass. A small banner popped up over each one:

> **UNIT: SHADOW CLONE — Movement 2 — Strength 4 — Upkeep: Ramen (1)**

Lilac stared. "You just *made units.*"

"Ha! Free scouts!" The real Naruto pumped his fist. "Okay, guys, spread out! North, east, south!"

"Yessir!" The clones ran off in three directions and vanished into the fog of war.

Lilac crossed her arms with a smirk. "Fine. Not bad. But the game charged you ramen upkeep."

"...Wait, *what?*"

---

## **TURN 3 — 3920 BC**

The clones came back with news. Well, two of them did.

"Okay, so," Clone #1 panted, "there's a city-state to the east. Super friendly. They gave me a free bowl of rice!"

"There's a big forest to the south," said Clone #2. "Also a goody hut! Some ancient ruins!"

"Where's the third one?" Lilac asked.

Both clones looked uncomfortable.

"...Barbarians," said Clone #1.

> **Your unit SHADOW CLONE has been destroyed by a BARBARIAN BRUTE.**

Naruto winced as the memory hit him. "Ugh. Big guy. With a club. And a really bad attitude."

Lilac's eyes narrowed. "Where's their encampment?"

"North, near the hills. Three tiles out, maybe?"

"Then they'll be heading our way soon." Lilac rolled her shoulders, and the air around her hummed faintly. "Good thing I don't need to be *built* to fight."

Naruto blinked. "You're gonna fight them?"

"I've fought a giant mech, an alien warlord, and an evil robot army. A guy with a club is a *Tuesday* for me."

Naruto stared at her for a second, then started grinning. "Okay, that's actually really cool."

Lilac felt her face warm. "It's... yeah. Just stuff I do."

"No, seriously! You just said it like it was nothing! That's so—" He stopped, coughed, and looked away. "So, uh. Tactical."

"...Tactical," Lilac repeated.

"Super tactical."

Clone #2 leaned toward Clone #1 and whispered, very loudly, "*Boss is being weird.*"

The real Naruto's face went bright red. "**DISMISSED!**"

*POOF. POOF.*

> **Ruins explored by SHADOW CLONE before dispersal: +25 Gold!**

"Hey, at least they did something," Lilac giggled.

---

## **TURN 4 — 3880 BC**

The barbarian brute came over the hill at dawn, just like Lilac had predicted. Two more followed him, carrying spears and shields.

> **⚠ BARBARIANS SPOTTED NEAR SHANG LEAF**

The settlers, who had become citizens and were very worried about it, huddled behind the wooden walls.

"Three of them," Naruto said, cracking his knuckles. "One for you, two for me?"

"Two for me, one for you," Lilac said. "You lost a clone yesterday."

"That was a *scouting* clone! They don't count!"

"Mm-hm."

The brute raised his club. "RRAAAGH!"

Lilac moved first. She dashed forward in a blur of purple, and the moment she crossed onto the next tile, the game *strained* to keep up.

> **SASH LILAC — Movement: ??? — Strength: ???**

"**Dragon Boost!**"

She shot across the plains and slammed into the first barbarian. He spun like a top and dropped. She looped back with her hair-whips cracking and knocked the spear out of the second one's hands.

"Hey! Save me some!" Naruto charged in. "**Shadow Clone Jutsu!**"

Five Narutos surrounded the last brute.

"Uzu—"
"—ma—"
"—ki—"
"**NARUTO BARRAGE!**"

The brute flew backward over the hill. A sad little popup followed him.

> **BARBARIAN BRUTE defeated! +5 Gold.**

The clones cheered and vanished. Lilac and Naruto stood next to each other on the hilltop, catching their breath while the morning sun turned the river gold.

"Not bad," Lilac said, nudging him with her elbow. "Ninja."

"You too, Dragon." He nudged her back, then hesitated. "Hey... is it weird that I'm kind of glad I didn't end up here alone?"

Lilac's ears twitched. She looked at the city below them: small, new, a single banner flapping in the wind. Then she looked at him.

"No," she said quietly. "Not weird."

Their hands brushed. Neither of them pulled away.

Then a new message slammed into the sky:

> **GANDHI of INDIA has met you!**
> *"Greetings, new friends. Let us walk the path of peace together."*

Naruto squinted at the tiny smiling portrait. "He seems nice."

Lilac shuddered for a reason she couldn't explain. "...Let's research Bronze Working next."

"Why?"

"Just a feeling."

> **END OF TURN 4.**
> **Shang Leaf — Pop. 1 | Gold: 30 | Science: Mining (2 turns)**
> **Next Turn: 3840 BC**

---

**To be continued in Turns 5–8...** 🐉🍥

Want me to keep going? Next up could be founding a second city, Naruto discovering that Ramen is somehow a luxury resource, or Lilac's friends Carol and Milla turning up as a rival civ.
